title: Security pen test & patching / SDLC review - Nova Financial
topics: Secure SDLC and code review cadence
Patching windows and emergency CVE response
Data residency and private deployment options
summary: Redwood and Nova Financial reviewed recent pen test findings, prioritized remediation for 2 high/7 medium/18 low issues, discussed integration into Nova's vulnerability management workflow, agreed on patching cadence, and reviewed Redwood's encryption/KMS and audit logging capabilities. Action items assigned for evidence exchange, remediation plan, and follow-up in 2 weeks.
header:
Date: 2026-05-10
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Alyssa Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Leah Park (Redwood CSM), Priya Kapoor (Nova Head of InfoSec), Ethan Miles (Nova Platform Eng), Sanjay Patel (Nova Security Analyst)
Recording: enabled
Files shared: pen_test_results_v2.pdf (link), SOC2-summary.pdf (link), remediation-tracker.xlsx (link)
transcript:
[00:00] Alyssa Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh this is Alyssa from Redwood. We also have Marco our SE and Leah on the call.
[00:12] Priya Kapoor: Hi all, thanks. We ran through the pen test last week and wanted to go through findings, patch cadence and how this ties into your SOC2 evidence.
[00:23] Marco Ruiz: Great, yeah thanks Priya. We reviewed the PDF you sent. Quick note — couple of typos in tool names in the report, some references to Redwoood runtime, you know small transcription, but the findings are clear.
[00:38] Ethan Miles: Quick context, Nova runs Redwood in a dedicated VPC with VMs in us-east-1 and we have monthly patching windows but we want to see if we need faster cadence for infra and model serving.
[00:52] Alyssa Chen: Understood. High level: pen test produced 2 high sev, 7 medium, 18 low. The two high ones were around an exposed metadata endpoint in an older image and one RCE vector in a third-party dependency patchable to 2.14.1.
[01:15] Sanjay Patel: Right, the RCE is CVE-2026-1452 right — that's the one we flagged as critical because we could chain it to access the container runtime.
[01:26] Marco Ruiz: That's the one. Our runtime team already did a mitigation patch and rolled a hotfix last night for hosted and dedicated images; for private installs we published guidance and a backpatched image.
[01:39] Priya Kapoor: Ok we need remediation evidence for SOC2. Can you provide the commit IDs, CVE references and timeline?
[01:48] Leah Park: Absolutely, we'll share the remediation tracker with commit hashes and patch dates. We can also provide the pen test triage notes.
[02:01] Priya Kapoor: On vulnerability management, Nova requires triage within 48 hours for critical/high and 7 days for medium. What's Redwood's SLA for critical CVEs?
[02:12] Marco Ruiz: Typical SLA is 24-72 hours to ship mitigations for critical, depending on repro and customer environment. For dedicated and private customers we prioritize and can schedule hot-fix images in under 24 hours for confirmed exploits.
[02:27] Ethan Miles: And how do you handle emergency patching for private deployments? Do we need to apply images ourselves or do you push?
[02:35] Alyssa Chen: For private deployments, we publish the backpatched image and an orchestration playbook. We can optionally run a short assist window with our solutions team if you enable secure tunnel access.
[02:48] Sanjay Patel: What's required for that tunnel? We have strict change control and need to log the session.
[02:54] Marco Ruiz: We use ephemeral SSH bastion access with session recording, and we can integrate session logs into your SIEM. We'll include the audit log entries as part of the evidence bundle.
[03:08] Priya Kapoor: Audit logs — how granular are they for model inference? We need token-level activity, route-level requests, and admin changes for SOC2.
[03:19] Alyssa Chen: Our audit logs include request metadata (timestamp, route, model id, user token id, source IP), admin actions (deploy, rollback, config change), and key operations (KMS rotate). For token-level cost/latency we can provide aggregated or request-level logs depending on retention tier.
[03:37] Ethan Miles: Data residency: Nova needs EU-only data processing for EU customers. Can you confirm regions and where KMS keys are stored?
[03:45] Marco Ruiz: Yes, for Nova we run nodes in eu-west-1 for EU data and keys live in the customer's KMS or a dedicated HSM per the private deployment. We support KMS BYOK and HSM-backed keys for on-prem.
[03:59] Priya Kapoor: Good. On the remediation plan, we want to attach each finding to your SDLC and release process so auditors see the path to fix. How do fixes propagate through dev/test/staging/prod?
[04:12] Marco Ruiz: We follow a git-flow style with CI gating, automated tests, and a canary rollout for infra changes. Hotfix images go through a minimal CI, a canary subset, then full rollout. We keep change records and link them to JIRA tickets; we'll export that as auditor evidence.
[04:35] Sanjay Patel: About the RCE, do you have a timeline for full eradication and a post-mortem?
[04:42] Marco Ruiz: Mitigation rolled out yesterday; full eradication includes replacing the vulnerable dependency across all layers, expected within 72 hours. We'll produce a short post-mortem doc.
[04:54] Priya Kapoor: Patching cadence — Nova policy wants at least monthly patching for infra and weekly for critical libraries. Can Redwood support weekly dependabot-style alerts and a prioritized patch plan?
[05:06] Alyssa Chen: Yes. We can subscribe your security team to our security mailing list and set up an automated dependency alert feed. We also provide a remediation tracker CSV that maps CVEs to releases and recommended action.
[05:20] Ethan Miles: Are there automated tests we can run to validate we aren't regressing model outputs when applying patches, especially quantization kernels?
[05:30] Marco Ruiz: We have a lightweight regression harness that runs smoke checks against a golden prompt set. For customers with Redwood Optimize, we can run a fuller eval to confirm output quality and recommend quantization profiles.
[05:45] Priya Kapoor: For SOC2 evidence — do you provide the control descriptions for RBAC and SSO? We need examples: SAML integration, SCIM provisioning, admin role matrix and separation of duties.
[06:01] Alyssa Chen: Yes we have an SSO guide with SAML examples and SCIM config. RBAC is role-based with admin/ops/dev/data roles and we support custom roles. We export role assignment reports for auditors.
[06:18] Sanjay Patel: Do you support MFA enforcement for admin accounts?
[06:22] Marco Ruiz: Yes, MFA is required for all admin and privileged accounts; we also integrate with IdP MFA policies.
[06:30] Leah Park: Quick note — we also attach our SOC2 Type II report and ISO 27001 attestation; we'll put links in Slack after the call.
[06:40] Priya Kapoor: Perfect. For vulnerability management we need to integrate your findings into our Jira board. Can you export the remediation-tracker.xlsx into Jira tickets?
[06:49] Marco Ruiz: We can provide CSV/Jira issue templates and optionally create tickets with your API token if you authorize it.
[06:58] Ethan Miles: What about long-tail low severity issues — do you have a backlog policy?
[07:03] Alyssa Chen: We triage low severity into quarterly backlog sprints; medium go into next-release lanes, high/critical trigger hotfix lanes. We'll mark each finding with proposed SLAs in the tracker.
[07:16] Sanjay Patel: Auditor will ask about patch testing; show us your test matrix for kernel changes.
[07:22] Marco Ruiz: We'll share an anonymized test matrix that lists functional tests, perf regression tests, and canary thresholds used during rollout.
[07:34] Priya Kapoor: Also need to confirm logging retention and WORM for audit artifacts for 3 years. Is that supported?
[07:42] Leah Park: Our premium retention tier supports 3+ years of immutable logs and export to your S3 with WORM policy. We'll include the export instructions.
[07:54] Priya Kapoor: Great. Next steps?
[07:57] Alyssa Chen: Recap: we'll send remediation artifacts (commit IDs, hotfix images), SOC2/ISO links, remediation tracker, and can create Jira issues if you provide a service account. We'll schedule a follow-up in two weeks to validate patches and review post-mortem.
[08:12] Priya Kapoor: Sounds good. Anything else from Nova?
[08:15] Ethan Miles: Please include instructions for encrypted backup rotation and key rotation schedule.
[08:20] Marco Ruiz: Noted — we'll include KMS rotation docs and recommended cadence.
[08:25] Alyssa Chen: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up over email with the artifacts and proposed dates.
[08:30] Priya Kapoor: Thanks all.
[08:33] (call ends)
